disease_label_per_paper: Disseminated Nocardia farcinica Infection in a Renal Transplant Patient: A Case Report
presentation_summary: Renal transplant recipient on tacrolimus, mycophenolate, and prednisone initially presented with fever, tachycardia, right flank pain, nausea, leukocytosis, neutrophilia, lymphopenia, high CRP, and right lower-lobe infiltrate/consolidation.
He later returned with malaise, anorexia, nausea, orthostasis, 15 kg weight loss over two months, left-sided throbbing headaches, unsteady gait, and loss of balance.

Imaging showed persistent right lower-lobe infiltrate, a round right lower-lobe mass, multiple bilateral lung nodules, and CNS lesions in the cerebellum and left parietal lobe that were later recognized as abscesses.
Brain abscess Gram stain showed gram-positive filamentous rods consistent with Nocardia, later identified as Nocardia farcinica with susceptibility guiding therapy.

quality_warnings: Microbiology, species identification, and susceptibility are confirmatory/treatment-context findings rather than ordinary observations.

Initial exact temperature and heart rate values were not reported; fever and tachycardia are represented through fever_history_activity and narrative risk context rather than fabricated numeric vitals.

Some laboratory values were reported during the initial febrile presentation, while CNS dissemination became clinically clear later; both are preserved as available clinical evidence from the same case trajectory.
